werk-cli-link: `werk link` and `werk unlink` add or remove one typed link between two cards

why: Deciding is the one state change the contract gates, so the command that makes it is where each missing fact is reported and fixed.

```
werk status <id> decided
```

The command moves a card to decided only if the four facts hold (#werk-contract-facts). It checks the log, not the card text.

- A missing fact makes the command fail. The message names the command that fixes it, with the card id filled in (#werk-contract-fix).
- `who`, the basis flag and the unchallenged flag are set with `werk edit` (#werk-cli-edit).
- A kill criterion is recorded with `werk kill` (#kill). One call adds one criterion.
- On a ghost, the check runs against the held edges, so the card commits as one unit (#werk-propose-new).
- `werk rederive <id> --status decided` runs the same check (#rederive-reason).
- The command never changes the text of a card (#map-frozen).
- A card whose depends_on target or parent is open or stale waits. The command fails and names that basis. It does not mark the card stale (#map-wait).

  -> refines         werk-cli  The CLI is the agent's interface to the map, and each verb belongs to the card that defines its operation
  -> depends_on      werk-contract-facts  A card needs four facts before it is decided
       why: The command reports and records the four facts that #werk-contract-facts lists.
  -> depends_on      werk-contract-fix  A failed check prints the exact next command
       why: The failure message of the command is the fix message that #werk-contract-fix defines.
  -> depends_on      werk-propose-new  A new card is a proposal too, not a direct append
       why: The check on a ghost runs against held edges because #werk-propose-new holds them.
  -> depends_on      werk-cli-edit  werk edit sets who, --no-basis and --unchallenged on a card without recreating it
       why: The decide command points at edit for the flags that record a missing fact.
  -> depends_on      map-wait  A card on a stale basis waits. It is not stale
       why: The command fails for a card that waits on its basis, as #map-wait defines.

card vi-onview  [decided]
One view = one card, detail on top, sub-cards below
why: No side panel. Every node has a page. The shape is identical at every depth.
subtree: 7 cards, 1 open, 6 decided, 1 unchallenged

Every card has one page, and every page has one shape. The detail of the card is on top. The sub-cards of the card are listed below it. The root, a leaf, and a source node use the same shape, so a reader learns the layout once.

The page has no side panel. To go deeper, the reader opens a sub-card, and the sub-card gets the same page. A leaf has no sub-cards, so its detail fills the page.

The address bar names the open card. A view can be shared, and it stays after a reload.
